name: Gentamicin creatinine-clearance PK reference curve (Duong 2022 / Bos 2019)
statement: Reference points are the deterministic predictions of the published Duong 2022 (Bos 2019 structural) one-compartment gentamicin population PK model, evaluated at the published cohort descriptors contained in this file. They are NOT raw patient observations; no residual noise has been added. The regression target is therefore exact parameter recovery, and agreement between optimised and published parameter values is the validity check.

published_residual_error.note: Recorded for provenance only; deliberately NOT applied to the reference curve.

sources.role: parameter values (Table S2, Bos row) and cohort descriptors (Table 1)
sources.citation: Duong A, Simard C, Williamson D, Marsot A. Model Re-Estimation: An Alternative for Poor Predictive Performance during External Evaluations? Example of Gentamicin in Critically Ill Patients. Pharmaceutics 2022;14(7):1426.

sources.role: structural model and residual error magnitudes (Table S1)
sources.citation: Bos JC, Prins JM, Misticio MC, Nunguiane G, Lang CN, Beirao JC, Mathot RAA, van Hest RM. Population pharmacokinetics with Monte Carlo simulations of gentamicin in a population of severely ill adult patients from sub-Saharan Africa. Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2019;63(4):e02328-18.

external_validation.role: External consistency check ONLY. Not read by evaluator/judge.mjs and not part of the metric.
external_validation.citation: Veinstein A, Venisse N, Badin J, Pinsard M, Robert R, Dupuis A. Gentamicin in hemodialyzed critical care patients: early dialysis after administration of a high dose should be considered. Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2013;57(2):977-982.
external_validation.note: Anuric/near-anuric ICU patients on intermittent haemodialysis; CrCl is not reported, so this cohort cannot constrain the CrCl slope. It is used to corroborate the model's implied non-renal clearance: extrapolating the published relation to CrCl = 0 gives 0.513 L/h = 8.5 mL/min, against the independently published population estimate CL_NHD = 0.1205 mL/min/kg (Table 4) = 9.1 mL/min at the cohort mean weight of 75.6 kg.
external_validation.transcription_check: Eight of nine summary columns reproduce the paper's printed Mean +/- SD exactly. CL_HD does not: the ten printed per-patient values give 74.72 +/- 23.57 mL/min against a printed 76.5 +/- 23.1, an inconsistency in the source. CL_HD is not used by any check.

cohort.description: Critically ill adult ICU patients (Quebec, Canada): HSCM n=39 and IUCPQ n=48.
